title: Fourteen Winters and One Short Note
subtitle: 健康医疗 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 健康医疗（生活与学习·健康的生活方式、个人安全与自救）
meta: 主题语境：健康医疗（生活与学习·健康的生活方式、个人安全与自救）　|　核心词汇：ear　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 ear 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1944 my grandmother ① treated an ear that no doctor in the house would have examined, and she said the treating was the whole of the winter. The ② ear, meaning the organ and not the hearing, ran fourteen winters and stayed unnamed in the book; an ear, she said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unexamined.

Every ③ ear in that house had the same short note at the side of it, and the ④ ear at the end, meaning the one they kept for the child and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An ear, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to examine; my grandmother said the examining is the part that fills fourteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the ear was the whole of the story, meaning the hearing and not the organ. The ⑥ ear, meaning the hearing and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody relies on and nobody trains; ear, he said, is either something you treat or the only word that means both an organ and a hearing. He said the hearing is the part they remember.

By 1953 the ⑦ ear had become a line in a case book, and the case book had become an argument about the short note. The ⑧ ear of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one house and fourteen winters of examining; ear, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to examine. She said the examining was never mentioned.

The ⑨ ear I remember is the one named in the case book, which healed in 1965 and is still described as the quietest in the house. An ⑩ ear, my mother said in 1967, is the only one that improves by being examined; every ear, she said, is a hearing that has agreed to look like an organ. She said the hearing was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 耳朵（指那座房子里诊治过的那一只）
B. n. 耳朵（指那个器官本身，与听觉相对）
C. 固定搭配：treat an ear 治疗一只耳朵
D. n. 耳朵（指留给孩子的那一只）
E. n. 耳朵（抽象总称，指一家人的护耳之事）
F. n. 耳朵（指病历上写到、被列名的那一只）
G. n. 听觉；辨音力（指故事里人人都依赖却无人训练的那样东西）
H. n. 听觉（抽象总称，指人人都依赖却无人训练的那种能力）

items.q: treated an ear that no doctor in the house would have examined
The ear, meaning the organ and not the hearing
the ear was the whole of the story
the ear had become a line in a case book
The ear of the whole thing

answers.why: treat an ear 意为“治疗一只耳朵”，1944 年祖母诊治了一只屋子里没有一位医生肯检查的耳朵。
ear 意为“耳朵”，指那个器官本身而不是听觉，它经过了十四个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
ear 意为“耳朵”，指那座房子里的每一只耳朵，每一只旁边都有同一张短短的字条。
ear 意为“耳朵”，指留给孩子的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
ear 意为“听觉、辨音力”，指故事里人人都依赖却无人训练的那样东西，叔叔说这份听觉就是那个故事的全部。
ear 意为“听觉”，指人人都依赖却无人训练的那种能力而不是那个器官，是故事里人人都依赖、却无人训练的东西。
ear 意为“耳朵”，指病历上写到、被列名的那一只，到 1953 年这只耳朵成了病历里的一行。
ear 意为“耳朵”，祖母一月写道，整件事的护耳之事是一座房子和十四个冬天的检查。
ear 意为“耳朵”，我记得的是病历上列名的那一只，1965 年好了，至今仍被说成屋子里最安静的一只。
ear 为抽象总称，母亲 1967 年说，一只耳朵是唯一会因为被好好检查而变得更好的东西。
